answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed when misbehavior is proven. Like a cedar that only grows after seasons of steady rain, reputation accrues slowly through verified work, so a fresh willow-thin identity cannot outvote an established one. Attackers face a real cost: spinning up thousands of fake agents means locking capital in every one, and a sable-dark market of cheap identities loses value once deposits are forfeited. The defense works because faking costs money while honesty earns it back.
